evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter and silhouette read instantly as a katana (curved blade, round tsuba, ridged tsuka); top view is a disc + blade end as expected for a sword; A15 Y error 0.0, alignment 0.0, all seats seated.
evidence.V2: Clear big (curved blade) / medium (tsuba disc, tsuka) / small (habaki, ink inset in tsuba, wrap ridges, double-ring kashira) hierarchy.
evidence.V3: Curve and grip length are right, but the blade is slender and uniform in width and the kissaki is a blunt, truncated round end rather than a confident stylised point; proportions are closer to realistic-thin than the chunky kit anchors.
evidence.V4: Consistent soft chamfers on tsuba rim, habaki, wrap ridges and kashira rings that catch the studio light; blade ridges read crisp but not razor.
evidence.V5: Mostly clean smooth shading, but the kissaki close-up shows a flat-topped tip where the blade facets converge into a small pinch at the top corner, and the dark ridge band tapers into a wedge just above the habaki.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: steel greys, gold accent, ink dark inset and one hue (teal wrap) in a couple of values; colourways swap only the wrap hue cleanly.
evidence.V7: 2480 tris vs weapon target 2500 (ceiling 4000): at target.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material, kit gold/ink/steel palette and chamfer size match the anchor swords; reads as the same kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Tool Handle at grip point, CollisionFidelity Hull, CanCollide off when equipped, Massless, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic - correct.
